WITH lines AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_key,
    sc.country_name AS store_country,
    cc.country_name AS cust_country
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS st
    ON s.store_key = st.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS sc
    ON st.country_code = sc.country_code
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS cu
    ON s.customer_key = cu.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS cc
    ON cu.country_code = cc.country_code
), both_store AS (
  SELECT
    product_key
  FROM lines
  WHERE
    store_country = 'Germany'
  INTERSECT
  SELECT
    product_key
  FROM lines
  WHERE
    store_country = 'France'
), both_cust AS (
  SELECT
    product_key
  FROM lines
  WHERE
    cust_country = 'Germany'
  INTERSECT
  SELECT
    product_key
  FROM lines
  WHERE
    cust_country = 'France'
)
SELECT
  p.product_name AS product,
  (
    p.product_key IN (
      SELECT
        product_key
      FROM both_store
    )
  ) AS shop_reading,
  (
    p.product_key IN (
      SELECT
        product_key
      FROM both_cust
    )
  ) AS customer_reading
FROM contoso_served.dim_product AS p
WHERE
  p.product_key IN (
    SELECT
      product_key
    FROM both_store
  )
  OR p.product_key IN (
    SELECT
      product_key
    FROM both_cust
  )
ORDER BY
  p.product_name

body.value: 1,840 rows came back, one per product that is sold in both Germany and France under at least one reading of "in a country", each carrying the product's name and two flags for which reading puts it there. 1,437 of them are flagged under both readings — a German shop and a French shop each rang the product up, and German-resident and France-resident customers each bought it. The remaining 403 are flagged only on the customer reading: bought by customers in both countries, but never by both countries' shops. No money and no units are in these rows, and no period was cut: each row asserts only joint presence in two countries' assortments over the whole order history 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. What I did NOT include: products sold in only one of the two countries or in neither, any per-country sales figure, any brand or category rollup, and any narrowing to a recent window.

value: Which "sold in Germany and France" did you mean — the shop that sold it, or the customer who bought it? I built both lists and will not choose between them, because they are different lengths. (a) SOLD BY OUR GERMAN AND FRENCH SHOPS — a shop in Germany rang it up and a shop in France did too: 1,437 products. (b) SOLD TO GERMAN AND FRENCH CUSTOMERS — a customer living in Germany bought it and a customer living in France bought it, web-shop orders included: 1,840 products. The fork cuts between colour variants of the same model, so it is not a cosmetic difference: of the first few rows alphabetically, "A. Datum Advanced Digital Camera M300" in Azure, Green and Grey is on BOTH lists, while the same camera in Black and Orange is on list (b) only. WHAT THE CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE: all 1,437 products on list (a) are also on list (b), so choosing never drops a product — it only decides whether 403 further products join, and those 403 reached both countries' customers only through the web shop, which carries no country of its own. It also does not change the period (all time, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, on order date), the grain (one row per SKU; names are unique 1:1 with product keys, so the list is faithful), or the starting set (all 2,517 catalogue products have sold somewhere). Say "shops" for the 1,437 or "customers" for the 1,840 and I will hand you that list of names.

All 223,974 served sales lines over the full order_date extent 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31 — because order.default.an_unscoped_question_covers_all_time (confidence C, operator ruling 2026-09-30) and the question named no period — inner-joined to dim_store, dim_customer, dim_country and dim_product on the declared foreign-key predicates, reduced to product grain and intersected within each reading. TWO POPULATIONS, deliberately both, which is why I return a choice and not a single list: the shop reading reaches only the 130,424 lines rung up at a physical store, because the web shop's store row carries the '--' country sentinel and so can never equal 'Germany' or 'France' — that exclusion falls out of the country equality itself, not from any channel filter I applied; the customer reading reaches all 223,974 lines, the 93,550 online ones included, since every line has a resident buyer. I applied no channel predicate (the subject is a Product, so store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel's `applies: subject` physical default does not reach this question), no store trading-state predicate, and no period filter. Set sizes: 1,437 products under the shop reading, 1,840 under the customer reading, the former a strict subset of the latter (store_list_only = 0, measured).

SELECT DISTINCT
  s.product_key,
  p.product_name
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON s.product_key = p.product_key

It is the set of sellable things with a sales record, not yet cut to any country — and it happens to be the entire catalogue, since no product in dim_product is unsold.

value.sql:
WITH lines AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_key,
    sc.country_name AS store_country,
    cc.country_name AS cust_country
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS st
    ON s.store_key = st.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS sc
    ON st.country_code = sc.country_code
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS cu
    ON s.customer_key = cu.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS cc
    ON cu.country_code = cc.country_code
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  product_key,
  'store' AS reading
FROM lines
WHERE
  store_country = 'Germany'
UNION ALL
SELECT DISTINCT
  product_key,
  'customer' AS reading
FROM lines
WHERE
  cust_country = 'Germany'
value.means: The products sold in Germany, counted twice over because "in Germany" has two meanings here and I am keeping both: 2,211 distinct products that a German SHOP rang up, and 2,390 distinct products that went to a customer who LIVES in Germany — one row per product per reading, over all 223,974 sales lines and the full order history 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. Neither figure is the answer to anything on its own; they are the two candidate German assortments that step 6 will intersect with France, and the overlap they lead to is 1,437 products one way and 1,840 the other.

readings.took: neither reading — both are carried forward, because the readings differ materially (1,437 vs 1,840 products in the final overlap) and the declaration explicitly forbids picking silently
readings.could_also_mean: the selling shop's country via store__trades_in__country (2,211 German products), or the buyer's home country via customer__based_in__country (2,390), or the site's country via location__in__country, which is the store's country one hop further out and gives the same cut
readings.declaration: country.default.whose_country_is_asked_never_assumed (confidence C, operator ruling 2026-10-22): never pick between the store and the customer silently, and never average the two

readings.took: the country literally named 'Germany' in dim_country.country_name, the declared reader-facing name column
readings.could_also_mean: nothing else — 'Germany' is one of the 9 stored values and is unambiguous; the '--' / 'Online' sentinel is not a country and cannot match
readings.declaration: country.exclusion.sentinel_is_not_a_country; dim_country.country_name is naming: long and the declared label for country_code

turns.why: Measure both declared readings of "sold in Germany" — the country of the shop it was rung up at, and the country the buyer lives in — and carry France through the same query so the fork is priced on the figure that actually matters, the size of the overlap.
